subjects.displayTitle: Welcoming many: growth through fellowship and service
subjects.introduction: Become the intimate companion of someone, ‘Abdu’l-Bahá says, guide them with proofs and with your own conduct, and before long souls will fly to the heights of guidance in successive waves. The promise that people will enter the religion of God in troops, drawn from the Qur’án, is answered everywhere in the Bahá’í writings with a demand on the present: act on even one Tablet, welcome, educate and sustain those who come, and let love be visible enough that an onlooker would want what the community has. Shoghi Effendi distinguishes a steady flow of new believers from the later entry by troops, and that from a mass conversion no one can yet picture, and warns that growth comes in surges of crisis and victory rather than at a uniform rate. Acts sets its numbers beside teaching, fellowship, prayer and provision for those in need [1], a reminder that enthusiasm becomes enduring participation only through shared life. The question is what a community must cultivate to be worth joining. From here the way leads into the growth of the Cause and into the Qur’án and Ḥadíth from which the phrase is drawn.
subjects.arc: Begin with personal companionship, widen the horizon of welcome, and distinguish promises of growth from the patient work that sustains it.

order.why: Read the image of shelter for all peoples.
shortened: This most powerful of dispensations will encompass all the earth, and beneath its banner will all peoples gather and be sheltered together.

order.why: Open with friendship, counsel, proof, and deeds as the conditions of welcome.
shortened: Each person must become the intimate companion of someone, guiding them through divine counsels, heavenly proofs, godly arguments, the way and conduct of those near to the Divine Court, spiritual qualities and pure and goodly deeds. If this is carried out, but a brief time will pass before souls will fly to the heights of guidance in successive waves.

order.why: Consider the reported challenge to put even one Tablet into practice.
shortened: But, by God besides Whom there is no other God, if the friends of God had acted according to what was revealed in just one of the Tablets of the Ancient Beauty, may His Most Great Mention be exalted, by now all who are on earth would have attained to the bounty of faith and the earth would have become the supreme paradise.

order.why: Widen the invitation to humanity beneath a canopy of unity.
shortened: Then you will observe how humanity will enter, group after group, beneath the canopy of the unity of the human world.

order.why: Connect expansion with each person becoming enkindled.
shortened: Soon most of the people of the world will become enkindled, for there has not been and is not any escape for anyone.

order.why: Bring prayer and enthusiasm into the work.
shortened: The cries of supplication and invocation will be raised to the Highest Kingdom therefrom and, verily, the people will enter into the religion of God by troops with great enthusiasm and attraction.

order.why: Meet discouragement with the promise of grace.
Consider growth despite trials.
shortened: But for this mighty Cause and momentous matter, despite storms and tempests, hurricanes and thunderbolts of tests and trials, people are entering into it in troops throughout all regions - east and west, south and north.

order.why: Distinguish gradual beginnings from later expansion.
Open the horizon of future centuries.
shortened: Its lustre, radiance and effulgence shall appear in future centuries when the signs of God will be spread abroad and the Word of God will encompass the hearts of all the peoples of the earth.

order.why: Read the comparison with Christianity’s small beginnings.
shortened: Eleven persons in the time of Christ became believers and were assured - now see what is happening: millions of bells ring out "O Christ! O Christ!" After a short time you will hear that from all regions the cry of "Ya Baha'u'l-Abha" is raised.

order.why: Keep the reported vision of widespread future participation.
shortened: Know this- that the Revelation of Baha'u'llah is the Word of God. There will not be a home which does not contain a believer. Look not at the present. Turn your vision upon the future. All the books written concerning the History of this Revelation number about fifty volumes.

order.why: Introduce the Quranic language of entry.
Read the expectation that its meaning will become clear.
shortened: The truth of the blessed verse "And thou didst see men entering the religion of God in troops" must become clear and evident.

order.why: Turn expectation into effort.
Retain the assurance of fulfilment.
shortened: Soon you will observe that the blessed verse "and they will enter the religion of God in troops" has been fulfilled.

order.why: Read the declaration of fulfilment in its own setting.
shortened: Today, praise be to God, "And thou seest men entering the religion of God in troops" has been fulfilled.

order.why: Consider the joy of a new morning.
shortened: Praise be to God, the sun of joy has risen and the lamp of gladness shines and the morn of truth has dawned and "they enter the religion of God in troops."

order.why: Close the linked readings with encouragement for a growing gathering.
shortened: This heavenly gathering will grow day by day, the intoxicated friends will increase in rapture and ecstasy, will break into songs and harmonies, and will raise such a melody as will reach the Supreme Concourse and rejoice and exhilarate the Holy Ones.

order.why: Retain the supplied report of future hosts.
shortened: Praise be to God that the sun of reality of religion hath dawned. From all parts of the world, host after host are coming under its radiance and ere long it will become world-spread.

order.why: Read the expectation of growth beyond present estimates.
shortened: Ere long the victory of the Kingdom will appear beyond all expectation, and "thou shalt see men enter the religion of God in troops" will be fulfilled.

order.why: Anticipates a portal opening through present darkness and people entering by troops.
Read the military imagery as part of the supplied spiritual exhortation.
shortened: It hath pitched its tents in the valley of existence with its forces and legions, and soon shall its spiritual armies seize the pillars of the world. Be thou numbered among this mighty host and charge forth with the power of meanings and wisdom upon the horizons of the nations.

order.why: Consider opening doors through purity and joy.
shortened: O thou cup overflowing with the Wine of the Love of God! Know thou that the doors of the Kingdom are being opened to both East and West. Verily, the people have remained heedless of the remembrance of their Lord after waiting for centuries and ages! However, those whose consciences are pure and whose hearts are sanctified hasten towards it and enter therein through every door with radiant faces and with hearts and spirits rejoicing.

order.why: Return to love as a condition of growth.
shortened: Be not perturbed, however; be firm and constant, for it is certain that a company of souls shall, with infinite love, arise to enter into the Kingdom of God.

order.why: Introduce the letter’s emphasis on unity and patience.
Read community action as a public example.
Consider what would make that example worth following.
Ask how love becomes visible to others.
Keep the letter’s account of maturity and social suffering in its historical context.
Distinguish the successive stages of expansion.
Read the warning that development will not be uniform.
Consider the implications of participation from diverse traditions.
Connect active preparation with sustaining the process.
End with spiritual effect rather than numerical achievement alone.

questions: What qualities would make someone feel both welcomed and able to contribute to a growing community?
How do these selections connect personal conduct with collective expansion?
What does the account in Acts add to a discussion of growth, shared life, and care for material needs?
How might a community prepare for greater participation while respecting different rates of response and learning?
What signs of deepening participation could help us assess growth beyond the number of people present?

neighbors.invitation: Consider enthusiasm expressed through conduct and clear speech.
Explore the kinds of education that continuing participation requires.

references.label: 1 · Acts 2:41–47 · A growing community’s shared life
references.note: Acts places numerical increase beside teaching, fellowship, prayer, shared resources, and attention to need. Compare those practices with the compilation’s emphasis on companionship and sustained participation, while keeping the two communities’ historical settings distinct.

subjects.displayTitle: Beyond discouragement: capacity, grace, and effort
subjects.introduction: Not every star can be of the first magnitude, ‘Abdu’l-Bahá once said, but each can shine where it is set; and not one of us can do everything, but everyone can cheer or comfort someone. That modest truth is the threshold to something far bolder. Look not to your own capacity, He writes again and again to people who had confessed their weakness, but to the grace of the Ancient Beauty, who can make an ant into a Solomon, a drop into an ocean, an atom into a sun, black soil into a garden. The blessings themselves create the worthiness; the very fact that someone has turned toward God is proof of a capacity they thought they lacked. None of this excuses the farmer from ploughing. Rain and seed need his labour, and the counsel is always to resolve, to pray for assistance and then to rise and begin, however small the gathering or weak the body. The same hope is owed to other people, whose capacities deserve the generosity we ask for our own. Paul, told that grace was sufficient and strength made perfect in weakness, found the same reversal at the heart of his faith [1]. The journey continues into divine confirmations, the development of capacity and readiness, and the differences in human capacity that grace does not erase.
subjects.arc: Start with a possible act of comfort, explore grace as the source of capacity, and bring confidence back to effort and generosity toward others.

order.why: Open with the reported assurance that everyone can comfort someone.
Contrast self-absorption with attention to divine gifts.
shortened: Look not to your own capacity and ability. Rather, look to the grace and bounty of the Ancient Beauty, Who can make an ant into a Solomon, and a drop into a vast ocean, Who can turn an atom into a sun and a mirage into a sweet flowing sea, Who can make black soil full of flowers and plants and a colorless stone into a royal pearl. If you look to His gifts and bounties, you will become the very essence of hope from head to toe, but if we look to ourselves, we become hopeless and despondent.

order.why: Introduce the claim that blessings themselves create worthiness.
shortened: Know that the blessings of the Kingdom of Abha are not dependent upon the capacity and the worthiness of any one; the blessings themselves are the worthiness. As the action itself, when it reaches the thing acted upon, makes it (that which is acted upon) the action,--so the blessings themselves then become identical with worthiness. In like manner, when the action itself descends upon the recipient, the recipient becomes the action.

order.why: Read capacity as dependent on bounty.
shortened: And do not look to lack of capacity or weakness of ability, for capacity and ability depend upon the bounty of your Lord, and your Lord's bounty has never been forbidden.

order.why: Compares personal capacity with a drop and divine bounty with an unlimited ocean.
Distinguish grace from personal merit.
shortened: O thou who art attracted to the Fragrances of God!
Consider not thy capacity and merit, nay rather consider the grace of thy Lord, the Clement, the Merciful.

order.why: Reinforce that distinction in another setting.
Consider turning toward God as an emerging capacity.
Apply hope to the capacities of other people.
shortened: O thou who art related to Fadl [Grace]!

This distinguished name means the manifestation of divine grace, and among its requirements is that in thy conduct, behavior and speech thou shouldst not consider the capacity and worthiness of people.

order.why: Balance rain and seed with the farmer’s work.
Connect prayer with resolve and action.
shortened: Whenever there is any work to be done and I see that physically I am not equal to it, I have just to resolve and supplicate Divine Assistance and arise in its performance. It will be done without delay.

order.why: Read the encouragement addressed to bodily weakness and limited thought.
shortened: In any case, do not look at your weak body and limited thoughts - look to the favors and bounties of the Lord of the Kingdom, for His confirmation is mighty and His power is without equal or likeness.

order.why: Keep the reported distinction between physical power and spiritual virtues.
shortened: The physical side of his life is weak and easily overcome but the ideal side of his life is the all-conquerer. The physical side of man is like an animal but the ideal aspect of his existence is humanistic - Physically man is aggressive, tyrannical, ignorant, overbearing, blood thirsty; - ideally he is just, gentle, wise, patient and benevolent.

order.why: Face the experience of personal hopelessness.
shortened: When I look to my own capacity and capability, I have no hope at all, but when I consider the divine confirmations and indubitable assistances of the Desired One, I see the gnat as an eagle and observe the mosquito with rainbow wings - and this is certain, absolute truth.

order.why: Turn from the dark lamp toward the sun.
shortened: If a lamp is extinguished and darkened, this has no bearing on the brilliant sun and radiant moon. Keep thy attention and vision fixed upon the sun, not the atom. Gaze upon the ocean, not the drop.

order.why: Read the reported contrast between self-regard and trust. Consider the reported experience of feeling useless.
Consider the drop’s relation to the ocean.
shortened: Let us not regard our own respective capacities; nay, rather, let us regard forever the favors and bounties of God. The drop must not estimate its own limited capacity; it must realize the volume and sufficiency of the ocean, which ever glorifieth the drop.

order.why: Read the promise of a drop becoming a sea.
shortened: Now we must not consider our ability and capacity, nay, rather, we must fix our gaze upon the favors and bounties of God, in these days, Who has made of the drop a sea, and of the atom a sun.

order.why: Keep the further reported transformation imagery.
Explore the ant and Solomon as images of unexpected capacity.
Read assistance as a power of change.
Consider the striking images of rain, flowers, and precious stones.
Return to the primacy of bestowal.
shortened: Look not to your own power and capacity - consider instead the bestowal of the Ancient Beauty, may my spirit be sacrificed for His teacher-believers.

order.why: Keep the reported assurance of bounty.
shortened: You must trust in the favors of the Blessed Beauty which can change a gnat into a phoenix, a drop into an ocean, a stone into a diamond and an atom into a world-illuminating sun. You must not look to your own capacities but to the bounties of the Abha Kingdom.

order.why: Read the exhortation to trust spiritual assistance.
shortened: The object which I wish to convey to you is this - you should not look at your capacity or ability, nay, rather, rely upon the confirmation of the Holy Spirit - do not doubt. Be confident and sure. It will help you.

order.why: Retain the concise reported encouragement.
Read the brief assurance of confirmation.
shortened: Do not look to your own capacity - look to the divine confirmations. If you arise to serve the Kingdom as you should and must, you will observe that the heavenly divine confirmations will arrive successively.

order.why: Place accomplishment in relation to confirmation.
shortened: Whatever occurred was His confirmation, else what capacity or power did we possess? Praise be to God, the Mighty Sovereign wages war with the hosts of the near angels and achieves great victories in East and West.

order.why: Consider the Quranic promise concerning those brought low.
shortened: They should not look to their own capacity, but rather rely and trust in the favors of the Lord of Majesty, so that they may become the dawning-places of lights and the manifestation of "We wish to show favor unto those who were brought low in the land, and to make them leaders, and to make them inheritors."

order.why: Read the reported example of a weak prisoner.
shortened: Do not look to your own capacity - divine confirmations will reach you. I was a weak imprisoned servant, but divine confirmations arrived.

order.why: Hear the particular encouragement to a woman arising in service.
shortened: In any case, O handmaiden of God, do not look to weakness and inability, but rather gallop in this field through the power of the love of God, and become the cause of enthusiasm and joy in Shiraz, that private chamber of mysteries.

order.why: Connect confidence with serenity and steadfastness.
shortened: Rely not therefore on thy capacities but in the effusive grace of the All Loving Lord and be firm at all times, be stalwart and serene in the Covenant and Testament.

order.why: Close the linked readings by turning attention toward constructive work.
shortened: If we do not like to associate with some people, very well, it is not compulsory. We can let them alone and become so busy with constructive work, that there is no time to waste upon such matters.

order.why: Read the historical reference to Bilal without adopting its racial rhetoric as an editorial judgement.
shortened: Look not to thine own capacity; rather, consider the divine bounty that can transform a drop into an ocean and make of a gnat a Solomon. He can cause Bilal the Habashi to excel over a Qurayshi chief, and make a Qurayshi Abu Lahab assume the features and disposition of a Habashi. This is not difficult for God.

order.why: Keep the reported excerpt and its visible omission.
shortened: Look upon the infinite Bounties of God. Do not look upon thine own incapability. Although the earth is the black soil, yet through the downpour of rain and the heat of the sun, flowers and anemones shall grow therefrom.

order.why: Retain the further supplied report with its source limitations.
shortened: Do ye not look upon your own capability and merit.
Therefore in this glorious Cause we must not consider our own capabilities but rather expect the Graces of God.

questions: How can honest recognition of a limitation differ from deciding that growth is impossible?
What relationship between grace and effort emerges from the farmer, seed, and rain?
How does Paul’s discussion of weakness illuminate or complicate these passages?
What might change if we approached other people’s capacities with the same hope encouraged for our own?
Which small, concrete act of comfort or service could become a starting point for developing a capacity?

neighbors.invitation: Explore the relationship between innate gifts and acquired perfections.
Connect renewed confidence with prayerful attention.

references.label: 1 · 2 Corinthians 12:9–10 · Grace and weakness
references.note: Paul describes Christ’s grace as sufficient and strength as perfected in weakness. Compare this reversal of ordinary self-sufficiency with the compilation’s assurances of assistance, then ask how each passage relates trust to the work still required.

subjects.displayTitle: A warmth others can feel: enthusiasm and spiritual life
subjects.introduction: Can a soul that has not itself come alive hope to revive another? ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s question sits at the centre of what it means to be enkindled. He describes the teacher’s fire in bodily terms, a bright face, clear speech, deeds that bear out words, a warmth that anyone who draws near can feel, and then surrounds those homely signs with larger images: a lamp, a vernal shower turning black soil into a rose garden, a second birth out of the womb of the world of nature. None of this is mere excitement. The flame is fed by purity of intention, by study in the school of the Covenant, by humility and supplication, and it is meant to pass from heart to heart until a whole gathering is warm. Luke tells of two disciples whose hearts burned within them as the scriptures were opened on the road [1], a reminder that understanding and inward fire belong together. Asking how such warmth is kindled and kept leads toward being a channel for the Holy Spirit, toward love understood as fire, toward teaching oneself first, and toward the confirmations that meet a heart already alight.
subjects.arc: Begin with enthusiasm made visible in conduct, explore the images of awakening, and return to gatherings, humility, and sustained practice.

order.why: Ground the flame in purity, peace, and work on oneself.
shortened: The aim is this: The intention of the teacher must be pure, his heart independent, his spirit attracted, his thought at peace, his resolution firm, his magnanimity exalted and in the love of God a shining torch. Should he become as such, his sanctified breath will even affect the rock; otherwise there will be no result whatsoever. As long as a soul is not perfected, how can he efface the defects of others? Unless he is detached from aught else save God, how can he teach severance to others?

order.why: Open with deeds, clear speech, and a happy face.
shortened: As to the fundamentals of teaching the Faith: know thou that delivering the Message can be accomplished only through goodly deeds and spiritual attributes, an utterance that is crystal clear and the happiness reflected from the face of that one who is expounding the Teachings. It is essential that the deeds of the teacher should attest the truth of his words.

order.why: Ask how one can awaken life without being inwardly alive.
shortened: Until such time, however, as the friends establish perfect unity among themselves, how can they summon others to harmony and peace?
"That soul which hath itself not come alive, Can it then hope another to revive?"

order.why: Directly identifies attraction, spiritual awakening and enkindlement as the power needed for teaching.
Read rebirth through knowledge and spiritual fire.
shortened: As regards the teachers, they must completely divest themselves from the old garments and be invested with a new garment. According to the statement of Christ, they must attain to the station of rebirth--that is, whereas in the first instance they were born from the womb of the mother, this time they must be born from the womb of the world of nature. Just as they are now totally unaware of the experiences of the fetal world, they must also forget entirely the defects of the world of nature. They must be baptized with the water of life, the fire of the love of God and the breaths of the Holy Spirit; be satisfied with little food, but take a large portion from the heavenly table.

order.why: Consider the reported connection with universal ideals.
shortened: Whosoever I send to America must at first gain the regenerative power of the second birth, be baptized with the water of universal ideals and be a living torch of the Fire of the Love of God.

order.why: Explore inner joy as a breath of life.
shortened: Whilst thou still hast breath within thy body, therefore, strive to abide in a state of enkindlement at all times, be sure to be in motion and inner joy at every moment of thy life.

order.why: Join radiance with understanding.
shortened: When a speaker’s brow shineth with the radiance of the love of God, at the time of his exposition of a subject, and he is exhilarated with the wine of true understanding, he becometh the centre of a potent force which, like unto a magnet, will attract the hearts. This is why the expounder must be in the utmost enkindlement.

order.why: Keep study and steadfastness beside enthusiasm.
shortened: In this Day, divine confirmations and assistance reach those who are enkindled in heart and soul, those who are studious in the school of the Covenant.

order.why: Balance intensity with mindfulness and supplication.
shortened: Be submissive and humble. Be enkindled and soul-consumed. Be mindful and suppliant.

order.why: Consider the warmth felt by people who draw near.
shortened: O servant of God! rejoice through the glad-tidings of God, be happy by the wafting of the fragrance of God, and cling to the Kingdom of God in such wise that it makes thee separate thyself from the world and kindle in thy heart the fire of the love of God to such an extent that any one who approaches thee will feel its warmth; and if thou desirest to attain to this station, thou shouldst turn thyself wholly unto God.

order.why: Read the influence of warmth among companions.
Follow the movement from one kindled heart to another.
shortened: God willing, may you ever abide beneath the shade of the providence of the Self-Sufficient, the Most High, and become so enkindled with the fire of the love of God that you may cause others to be set ablaze thereby.

order.why: Read greetings as a means of conveying warmth.
Return to teaching with a bright face.
shortened: Loose thy tongue and teach, and let thy face be bright with the fire of God's love.

order.why: Hear the exhortation addressed to women.
shortened: O handmaids of the All-Merciful! Through the favors and bounties of the Ancient Beauty, may my spirit be sacrificed for Him, it is hoped that each one of those handmaids of the All-Merciful will be so enkindled with the divine fire that she will illumine the world with the heat of the love of God, and will, through eloquent speech and fluent tongue and the confirmations of the Holy Spirit, expound the essence of divine explanation in such wise that the learned ones, the wise ones and the mystics of the earth will be amazed.

order.why: Consider the attraction of hearts.
shortened: One must become so enkindled with the fire of the love of God that hearts are completely attracted.

order.why: Connect illumination with activity.
Keep the reported link between love and progress.
shortened: If love did not exist, what of reality would remain? It is the fire of the love of God which renders man superior to the animal. Strengthen this superior force through which is attained all the progress in the world.

order.why: Consider the reported call for renewed thought and joy each day.
shortened: Every morning sing a new song and every evening think a new thought. Every day shed a new light over the dark minds of humanity and every hour cast a new joy in the minds of men. Let the pillars of the earth shake with the thunder of your voice and send a new reverberation through the columns of mankind.

order.why: Retain the reported candle imagery in its own setting.
shortened: Teaching is like unto a candle which is lighted in the soul of man; it is the Fire of the Love of God. When this condition of enkindlement is obtained, man becomes entirely unconscious and his words will penetrate through the rock.

order.why: Ask what atmosphere a person’s presence creates.
shortened: Similarly there are some enkindled souls whose very presence in a meeting changes its atmosphere, suffering the people to become truly spiritual, turning their faces towards God; others like unto the black smoke, darken the horizon of the minds.

order.why: Read the effect of one enthusiastic person upon companions.
Turn to the conditions of a warm and cheerful gathering.
Read the particular encouragement to communities in Canada.
shortened: Likewise in the provinces of Canada, such as Newfoundland, Prince Edward Island, Nova Scotia, New Brunswick, Quebec, Ontario, Manitoba, Saskatchewan, Alberta, British Columbia, Ungava, Keewatin, Mackenzie, Yukon, and the Franklin Islands in the Arctic Circle--the believers of God must become self-sacrificing and like unto the candles of guidance become ignited in the provinces of Canada. Should they show forth such a magnanimity, it is assured that they will obtain universal divine confirmations, the heavenly cohorts will reinforce them uninterruptedly, and a most great victory will be obtained.

order.why: Retain the recollection associated with Iraq.
Preserve the Sinai imagery and its supplied omission.
Read another image of Sinai’s fire.
Consider the burning away of obstructive imaginings.
Close the linked readings with the widening horizon of spiritual warmth.
shortened: I hope that through the invisible confirmations, thou mayest, from whatever door thou enterest, be confirmed and assisted, and become so enkindled with the fire of God as to set the world aflame.

order.why: Retain the supplied fragment about the teacher’s own response. End with humility beside the fire of devotion.
shortened: The teacher, when teaching, must be himself fully enkindled, so that his utterance, like unto a flame of fire, may exert influence and consume the veil of self and passion. He must also be utterly humble and lowly so that others may be edified, and be totally self-effaced and evanescent so that he may teach with the melody of the Concourse on highâ€"otherwise his teaching will have no effect.

order.why: Read the concise encouragement to radiance.
shortened: O thou radiant light! Every countenance that is illumined by the light of guidance is a luminous lamp, a merciful candle, and a heavenly star. Therefore, since thou hast been enkindled with the love of God, thou art radiant, brilliant and effulgent.

order.why: Connect the reading of verses with a glad spirit.
shortened: The leaves of the garden of the knowledge of God have unfurled, and hearts have been refreshed by their sweet fragrance, and breasts have been gladdened by the scent of its blossoms. And thou, O thou who art attracted by the verses of God, be thou gladdened in spirit, set ablaze in heart, and moved in soul by this breeze which hath wafted from it the fragrance of the Spirit.

order.why: Consider warmth and harmony in meetings.
shortened: How are the Believers? Are they enkindled? Are they brilliant stars in the Assembly? Do they serve the Cause of God in Love and Harmony? In the meetings of Believers is there a real quickening, or is it cold?

order.why: Read the reported contrast between learning alone and inward response.
shortened: A teacher like Esmollah Asdag was very enkindled. His talk effected the hearts of men, no matter how cold and indifferent. There were some amongst the believers who were most learned and erudite but because "the Flame of the Spirit" was not burning in their souls they could not teach one person. He had a very attractive, smiling, winsome face. Whenever he began to speak he himself was so stirred by the 'urge of the spirit' that the listeners were moved profoundly and accepted the Truth before he had come to the end of his talk.

order.why: Bring love into the opening of hearts.
shortened: By My life, whoso attaineth unto His knowledge soareth in the atmosphere of His love and detacheth himself from all who dwell on earth, let alone those who speak according to their desires that which God hath not permitted them.

Hear ye the voice of the Wronged One. Speak ye in the name of Truth, and be adorned with the ornament of His remembrance and illumined by the lights of His love. This is the key to hearts and the polish of existence.

order.why: Keep the supplied account of love’s heat.
shortened: O friends! Ye must all be so ablaze in this day with the fire of the love of God that the heat thereof may be manifest in all your veins, your limbs and members of your body, and the peoples of the world may be ignited by this heat and turn to the horizon of the Beloved.

order.why: Read the description of an entire body stirred to action.
shortened: O thou lamp who art enkindled with the fire of the Love of God! Verily, I read thy recent letter which showed thy strong love, thy being ablaze with the fire of the love of thy Lord, the Mighty, the Praised, and the penetration of the Spirit of Truth in thy limbs, nerves, veins, arteries, bones, blood and flesh, until it hath taken the reins of power from thy hands and moveth thee as it willeth, causeth thee to speak in what it willeth and attracted thee as it willeth. This is becoming of whatever heart is replenished with the spirit of the love of God.

order.why: Read the encouragement to travel and teach.
Explore the joined images of earth, fire, and breeze.
Connect vigour with understanding and righteous conduct.

questions: Which qualities distinguish nourishing enthusiasm from excitement that soon exhausts itself?
How do understanding, prayer, and work on oneself shape the warmth described here?
What does Luke’s account suggest about the relationship between interpretation, recognition, and an inward response?
How might a gathering welcome quiet forms of spiritual depth as well as expressive joy?
What would it mean for another person to recognize our conviction through the good it brings into their life?

neighbors.invitation: Begin renewed effort with the possibility of comforting someone.
Explore companionship and conduct as conditions of welcome.

references.label: 1 · Luke 24:30–32 · Hearts kindled through understanding
references.note: The disciples recall their inward response as Jesus opened the scriptures to them, in an account that also involves recognition and a shared meal. Compare that relationship between understanding and warmth with the compilation’s images of enlivening others; the comparison does not erase the narrative’s specifically Christian claims.

subjects.displayTitle: Learning to become: why capacities need cultivation
subjects.introduction: A flower does not reach its colour and charm by itself; it needs a gardener. ‘Abdu’l-Bahá begins with that observation and distinguishes two blessings, the capacity we are born with and the perfections we acquire, before asking what it takes to move from one to the other. Land left alone becomes a thicket of weeds; a lamp needs an igniter; seeds concealed beneath the earth stay seeds. Human beings require education that is material, intellectual and spiritual at once, and an educator equal to all three must be distinguished above all others, which is why the argument arrives at divine revelation. Yet the learner is no mere vessel: independence of a teacher is impossible, but perception and discovery remain one’s own, and the aim is understanding rather than dependence. Plato describes education as turning a power already present in the soul toward what it should see [1], a philosophical companion to this theology of cultivation. From here the way continues toward the Manifestation of God as educator, the education of children, and universal education as the means by which what is learned becomes a benefit to others.
subjects.arc: Begin with the distinction between innate gifts and acquired perfections, examine the work of education, and return to understanding, agency, and renewed life.

order.why: Lay out material, intellectual, and spiritual education. Revisit the power attributed to revelation.
shortened: It is therefore clear and evident that man stands in need of an educator. This educator must undeniably be perfect in every way and distinguished above all men. For if he were like others he could never be their educator, particularly since he must at once be their material, human and spiritual educator.

It has thus been established by rational arguments that the world of existence stands in utmost need of an educator, and that its education must be achieved through a celestial power. There is no doubt that this celestial power is divine revelation, and that the world must be educated through this power which transcends human power.

order.why: Open with innate capacity and acquired perfections as two blessings. Consider the diary account of education’s importance.
Introduce the lamp that needs to be kindled.
Read latent lights and seeds in need of cultivation.
Keep personal perception and discovery beside the need for teaching.
shortened: As to the question of souls' independence in receiving from the Sun of Reality, it is clear that all humanity needs education. Given this need for education, how can independence be conceived? Is it possible for any individual to acquire by himself, without a teacher, all human perfections? Thus independence is not possible. Yes, even while learning and receiving from others, man has his own feelings and perceptions and can make new discoveries, but he cannot dispense with teacher and educator.

order.why: Read the reported call to ascertain truth before following guidance.
Consider understanding as a mark of true teaching.
Explore a teacher’s part in awakening capacity.
shortened: He has capacity but needs a teacher to explain divine matters and open his eyes and ears as they should be opened.

order.why: Read the reported argument from our need for instruction.
Consider the relation between nature and education.
Read the historical cultivation analogy without turning it into an ecological judgement.
shortened: The purpose and object of schools, colleges and universities is to educate man and thereby rescue and redeem him from the exigencies and defects of nature and to awaken within him the capability of controlling and appropriating nature's bounties. If we should relegate this plot of ground to its natural state, allow it to return to its original condition, it would become a field of thorns and useless weeds, but by cultivation it will become fertile soil, yielding a harvest.
Therefore, it is not intended that the world of humanity should be left to its natural state.

order.why: Keep the further reported example of cultivation.
shortened: When we look upon the kingdoms of creation below man, we find three forms or planes of existence which await education and development. For instance, the function of a gardener is to till the soil of the mineral kingdom and plant a tree which under his training and cultivation will attain perfection of growth.
As to the human world: It is more in need of guidance and education than the lower creatures.

order.why: Consider capacities that require development.
shortened: God in his wisdom has created all things. Nothing has been created without a special destiny, for every creature has an innate station of attainment.
Each kingdom of nature holds potentialities and each must be cultivated in order to reach its fulfillment.

order.why: Read the reported emphasis on care for children.
Retain the reported comparison involving human impulses.
Connect childhood education with the example of the Prophets.
Read school and orchard as parallel images.
Consider assistance as a means of changing conditions.
shortened: Everything and every created being must have a guardian or cultivator to assist in making the change from one condition to the other. The flower requires the gardener. To change water into wine there must be someone to assist in the matter.

order.why: Distinguish visible neglect from less visible spiritual needs.
Keep the concise reported statement of universal need.
Read the reported link between wisdom and a teacher.
shortened: Therefore man needs a teacher; for, in order that he may acquire this perfection, some one must aid him in bringing it forth. The gaining of Wisdom requires a teacher.

order.why: Consider the argument for help beyond oneself.
Ask how guidance is received.
shortened: [One evening 'Abdu'l-Baha was in the little garden outside the house. A number of us pilgrims were present. Calling attention to trees and flowers He had planted, He said in part: "This was a place for dirt and refuse and loathsome to look upon. During the days when Akka was in confusion and the whirlwind of tests was violent, and a rumor persisted that they were about to banish us to a remote place, we were engaged in planting these trees and flowers, and laying out this garden. Now this has become such a delightful place. How surprising indeed is the assertion made by some people that existence needs no trainer! Were it not for the direct result of care and training, this place would have ever remained a heap of dirt and refuse." Then He walked toward the house, followed by us all. In the sitting-room, downstairs, He resumed the above conversation to the following effect:]

order.why: Introduce the Prophets as gardeners.
Read the role of Christ and the Prophets in educating hearts.
Retain the reported priority given to prophetic education.
Consider the continuing need for a universal impulse.
shortened: When asked if it would be always necessary for prophets to come from time to time -- "would not the world in the course of events through progress reach to a full realization of God?" -- Abdu'l-Baha replied: "Mankind needs a universal motive power to quicken it. The inspired messenger who is directly assisted by the power of God brings about universal results.

order.why: Explains the need for a universal educator through the analogy of officers and soldiers needing a commander.
Read teaching, wisdom, and purification together.
Keep the reminder of dependence within the image of infancy.
shortened: People are observed to be as infants - they need an educator and one who will remind them.

order.why: Read the reported rain-and-flowers analogy.
shortened: Consider how this black soil is decorated with multi-colored flowers through the Bestowals of the Sun, the downpour of the rain and the blowing of the winds! Although the earth was dark, yet through the benedictions of the four elements it was be gemmed with such fragrant roses! And produced such luscious fruits!

order.why: Consider the reported conversation between sun and earth.
Close the linked readings with prayer for renewed thought and purpose.
Retain the supplied report and its omission.
End with the development of divine perfections.
shortened: Among the proofs and arguments for the existence of God is the fact that man has not created himself, but rather that his creator and fashioner is another than he. And it is certain and indisputable that the creator of man is not like man himself, because a powerless being cannot create another being, and an active creator must possess all perfections to produce his handiwork.
Thus the contingent world is the source of deficiencies and God is the source of perfection. The very deficiencies of the contingent world testify to God's perfections.

questions: What is the difference between recognizing a person’s potential and helping that potential become effective?
How do material, intellectual, and spiritual education support or challenge one another?
Where does the learner’s own discernment enter these accounts of guidance?
How does Plato’s image of turning an existing faculty compare with the lamps and gardens in this compilation?
What qualities would make education a source of greater understanding and service rather than dependence on the educator?

neighbors.invitation: Consider cultivation as the meeting of assistance and effort.
Follow learning into the fruits of action.

references.label: 1 · Plato, Republic, Book VII · Turning the capacity to learn
references.note: In the discussion following the cave allegory, Socrates argues that education turns a capacity already present in the soul toward the good. Compare this with the compilation’s distinction between latent gifts and acquired perfections, while attending to their different accounts of the teacher and of ultimate knowledge.

subjects.displayTitle: Faith that deepens: conviction, assurance, and action
subjects.introduction: Faith and certitude, ‘Abdu’l-Bahá writes, are a tree in the garden, and good deeds are its fruit; that is the simplest test of how deeply a conviction has taken root. But faith also has an inward history. It can be inherited with one’s parents, grasped with the understanding, or lived in practice; it can be confessed with the tongue, believed in the heart, shown in action. Beyond belief there is assurance, the station Abraham sought when, already believing, he asked to see how God gives life to the dead so that his heart might be at rest [1]. Bahá’u’lláh describes seekers who recognized Him on merely hearing of Him, others who needed proofs and lingered, others who crossed the whole path in less than the blink of an eye; the path is one, and it differs with the capacity of the traveller. Such distinctions are tools for examining one’s own integrity and growth, not a scale for ranking other people, and certitude itself is called a bounty rather than an achievement. Where it leads is a life of service, trustworthiness and steadfast love. The journey continues inward to the inmost heart, to the spirit of faith, and to the transformation that walking the spiritual path brings about.
subjects.arc: Open with the fruits of faith, explore the distinctions among its stages, and bring assurance back to practice, fellowship, and continued growth.

order.why: Distinguish profession, inward response, and action in the reported account.
shortened: "Faith outwardly means to believe the Message a Manifestation brings to the world and accept the fulfillment in Him of that which the Prophets have announced.
But, in reality, Faith embodies three degrees: -To confess with the tongue; to believe in the heart; to give evidence in our actions. These three things are essential in true Faith.

order.why: Open with deeds as the fruit of faith.
shortened: O thou who art firm in the Covenant! Faith and certitude are like a tree in the garden, and praiseworthy deeds and actions mentioned in the Book are like its fruits.

order.why: Read the movement from inherited belief to understanding and practice.
Introduce assurance as a further deepening of faith. Read rational proof, seeing, and fulfilment as different modes of certainty.
shortened: The station of assurance is greater in degree than that of mere faith. It is the station denoted by "that they should add faith upon faith."

The grades of existence are finite but the perfections in each grade of existence are endless. Thus when He [Abraham] sayeth, "that my heart may have assurance" this is the station of the Knowledge of Certitude. This is a certainty that will be achieved with reflection and rational proofs. The Station of the Eye of Certitude is the station of beholding the lights of certainty. The station of the Reality of Certitude is the full realization of that certainty.

order.why: Read the reference to Abraham’s desire for a heart at rest.
shortened: Assurance is above faith, as evidenced in the blessed verse: "Dost thou not believe?" He said: "Yes, but that my heart may be at rest."

order.why: Consider faith and assurance as gifts.
shortened: O thou leaf that hath attained unto certitude! Souls there are many but assured souls are few and far between. For certitude is a bounty and a grace that cometh from God. "This is a bounty of God that He vouchsafeth to whomsoever He willeth". No soul is worthy of the divine threshold or can approach the Court of Abha Beauty unless he hath attained the station of certitude. A believer might have faith but he may not yet be assured; a soul may turn to God but he may not have attained the state of certitude.

order.why: Follow the sequence from seeking through firmness.
shortened: Among souls variations are observed: Some neither sought nor found; some sought but found not; some found without seeking yet did not arrive; some arrived but recognized not; some arrived and recognized yet afterwards became unsettled, for the root of the tree of knowledge was not firmly planted in their hearts - with the slightest breeze they were uprooted. But some, by God's grace, remained firm and steadfast. These are the gems of existence - upon them be the glory of God, His remembrance and His praise.

order.why: Recognize different routes and rates of response.
Keep differences of insight beside the warning against disputes.
Read the four stages associated with the heart.
shortened: But to this evanescent One of the mystic ocean, this station is the first gate of the heart's citadel, that is, man's first entrance to the city of the heart; and the heart is endowed with four stages, which would be recounted should a kindred soul be found.

order.why: Compare another description of four kinds of wayfarer.
shortened: 8 O my eminent friend! They that seek to ascend to the heaven of mystic wayfaring are of four kinds only. I shall describe them in brief, that the signs and degrees of each may become plain and manifest to thee.

order.why: Distinguish the oneness of essence and attributes.
Connect reflection upon oneself with certitude and recognition.
shortened: Man must reflect upon the Self of Truth. After attaining certitude, whatsoever He ordains is beloved and acceptable, and none may say why or wherefore.

order.why: Read purification of the channel and entry into the City of Certitude.
shortened: When the channel of the human soul is cleansed of all worldly and impeding attachments, it will unfailingly perceive the breath of the Beloved across immeasurable distances, and will, led by its perfume, attain and enter the City of Certitude.

order.why: Consider knowledge as a source of precious insight.
Read the invitation to drink from the ocean of certitude.
Consider doubt in the image of sun and darkness.
shortened: Say: This is the Sun of certitude which hath dawned from the manifest horizon. After its rising, is doubt befitting? Nay, by Him Who raineth down from the clouds!

order.why: Bring remembrance and the sweetness of utterance into the journey.
Retain the assurance of guidance.
shortened: O thou who art drawn near to the Divine Threshold! Good fortune and felicity made thee a recipient of divine bounties and illumined and enlightened thee with the light of guidance.

order.why: Connect progress through degrees with acquiring perfections.
Read daily progress in relation to gatherings and the heart.
shortened: Therefore, in thanksgiving for this great bounty and supreme triumph, you must advance day by day in the stations of certitude so that divine gifts may become fully manifest in luminous gatherings and the outpourings of the praiseworthy station may spring forth and flow from the essence of the heart.

order.why: Consider firmness in the Covenant.
shortened: Through the ancient grace of the Greatest Name (may my spirit be sacrificed for His loved ones), I hope they will be so firmly established in faith, certitude and the Covenant and Testament that they become manifest light from the highest horizon.

order.why: Read the distinction among responses and actions in its polemical setting.
Introduce the testing of faith and love.
Distinguishes differences in human degree from differences involving faith, certitude and response to divine love.
Read the reported claim that tests disclose what is present.
Consider the reported peace of certitude even in prison.
Keep the further reported passage and its omission.
Read the fragrance image as an expression of inward reality.
Connect fragrance with togetherness.
Close the linked readings with the reported garden that must be tended.
Compare the further threefold account.
shortened: Ponder attentively the accounts of the prophets and the Messengers of the past: how it was that they were calumniated against; in what manner they were treated; how it was that individuals became veiled from the Truth and were heedless of the Remembrance of their Lord. Do this until such time as He enableth the lights of Truth to shine upon thee, setteth thee apart from error, causeth thee to attain unto the station of the "knowledge of certitude" ('ilm al-yaqin), guideth thee unto the "essence of certitude" ('ayn al-yaqin) and causeth thee to realize the "reality of certitude" (haqq al-yaqin) through the bounty of the Manifest Light.

order.why: Retain the supplied progression and its boundary notice.
shortened: The station of certitude is above that of faith, and the truth of certitude [haqqu'l-yaqin] is above the knowledge of certitude ['ilmu'l-yaqin].  Now that thou hast drunk from the spring of certitude ['aynu'l-yaqin; also "eye of certitude"], thou shalt assuredly attain, through God's infinite bounties, unto the truth of certitude, that thou mayest become in both worlds the manifestation of endless favors.

order.why: Return to the reference to Abraham.
shortened: O God! O Thou Who givest life to the world and educates the nations! I beseech Thee by Thy Greatest Name to cast tranquility into the heart of Thy servant Hatam Muhammad, that his heart may find peace in Thy irrevocable Cause, for Thou hast placed the station of peace above faith, as Thou hast made clear in Thy Holy Book and Thy Mighty Qur'an, addressing Abraham: "Dost thou not believe?" He said: "Yes, but that my heart may be at rest." Thus didst Thou confirm his certain knowledge with the vision of certainty and the truth of certainty.

order.why: Keep the supplied invitation to drink within its source limits.
shortened: He, verily, is the Mighty, the All-Wise. Drink thou at all times from the choice wine of certitude, the seal whereof hath been broken by the finger of thy Lord, the Almighty, the All-Powerful.

order.why: Connect insight with wise utterance and effort.
shortened: God willing, may you attain in this precious and wondrous Day to the fragrances of the divine Robe. These fragrances are mentioned in one instance that has flowed from the Most Exalted Pen. By the sighs of this Wronged One! If anyone truly attains unto them, he will find himself detached and free from the world and all who dwell therein, and will arise to promote the Cause with perfect strength, power and steadfastness, occupying himself with the remembrance of the Beloved of all creation through wisdom and utterance.

order.why: Read the reported strengthening through trial.
Keep the further warning in its own polemical setting.
shortened: As for what thou hast written concerning the doubts that have come upon thee and thy brothers, this stems from thy station upon the carpet of nearness to thy Lord and Master. Therefore seek refuge in God, hold fast to His cord, and rely upon Him. Know that the limit of certitude is when thou fearest naught alongside God and seest no matter as significant beside God's grandeur. Any station below this is not of Us and cannot be attributed to Us, but rather originates from the depths of the darkness of self and returns thereto when not treasured.

order.why: Read the reported judgement about motives as a historical claim, not a licence to judge others.
shortened: When man has no faith, he becomes susceptible to all manner of evil and vice. Every wickedness may be expected of him, and even if a soul who is not illumined by the light of faith performs a good deed, it must surely be based on some ulterior motive or self-interest. Yet evil deeds are likely to proceed from him, unless he be fearful. Through fear of punishment and law does he avoid evil.

order.why: Return to the reported distinction between profession and lived example.
End with love deepened into lasting service.
Keep the provisional rendering of the same distinctions visibly separate.

questions: What kinds of fruit would help us recognize faith becoming more deeply lived?
How do the different accounts of stages or degrees illuminate one another without needing to form one identical sequence?
What does Abraham’s request suggest about the relationship between belief, questioning, and reassurance?
How might attention to the inmost heart and knowledge of oneself change the way we examine our convictions?
How can discussion of spiritual growth strengthen humility and fellowship rather than encourage ranking other people?

neighbors.invitation: Consider personal discernment within a life of learning.
Consider the desire and attentiveness involved in a search for truth.
Explore the inmost heart as a place of recognition and assurance.
Bring the examination of conviction into knowledge of oneself.

references.label: 1 · Quran 2:260 · Abraham seeks reassurance
references.note: Abraham affirms belief while asking to understand how God gives life to the dead, so that his heart may be at ease. Read the parallel translations, then compare the verse with the compilation’s distinction between faith and assurance. The verse itself is a narrative, not a complete taxonomy of spiritual stages.

subjects.displayTitle: Knowledge, authority, and the courage to recognize anew
subjects.introduction: By what proof did you believe before, Bahá’u’lláh asks the divines, and by what evidence do you now turn away? The question is addressed to those whose learning should have prepared them to recognise truth, and it exposes how the same learning, joined to status and inherited expectation, can become the thickest of veils. He tells them to judge with justice, to keep their faces turned toward the poor, to look at the signs with new eyes, and to remember that for centuries they prayed for the Promised One’s advent and then pronounced judgment against Him when He came. The language is fierce and belongs to particular confrontations; it is not a licence for contempt toward scholars or communities. Jesus’ rebuke of leaders who tithed mint and cumin while neglecting judgment, mercy and faith [1] makes a comparable demand on anyone who holds authority over others. The questions reach past formal leadership to each of us: whether our standards of evidence are consistent, whether we welcome correction, and whether knowledge enlarges our responsibility. From here the path leads to the proclamation addressed to Muslims, to the Christian clergy, to kings and rulers, and to the peoples of the world.
subjects.arc: Begin with justice and care, examine the standards by which claims are judged, and read the stern warnings as a demand for accountable spiritual leadership.

order.why: Invite a fresh way of seeing.
Open with justice and responsibility toward the poor.
Ask whether the same evidential standards are applied consistently.
shortened: Say: Be fair, O concourse of divines! By what proof did ye believe aforetime, and by what evidence do ye now turn away from this hidden Name?

order.why: Compare the grounds of former belief with present rejection.
shortened: O concourse of divines! By what proof did ye believe in My previous Manifestations yet deny this Manifestation at Whose appearance all things have cried out: "The Kingdom belongeth unto God, the Mighty, the All-Knowing"? Do ye imagine that ye are the beneficent? Nay, rather ye are among the most lost!

order.why: Read the question concerning belief in Muhammad.
shortened: Say: O concourse of divines! Ye are the veils of the earth and its doubts - to this testifies He with Whom is the perspicuous Book. Were ye to be fair, by what proof did ye believe in Muhammad, the Apostle of God, and by what evidence did ye turn away from Him Who came to you with that which is with the All-Knowing? Fear God and be not of the wrongdoers.

order.why: Consider the precedents of opposition to Jesus and Muhammad.
Read the invitation to reflect upon former persecution.
Bring fair judgement against the influence of fancies.
Keep the concise appeal to fairness.
Read the invitation to respond fairly to a new gift.
shortened: Say: O concourse of divines! Be fair in the Cause of God and His sovereignty, and follow not fancies and idle imaginings. Behold what hath been inscribed by the Most Exalted Pen upon the Tablet of existence. God hath come with manifest sovereignty. Cast away what ye possess and take what ye have been given from God, the Mighty, the Loving.

order.why: Hear the specific appeal to Persian religious leaders.
shortened: O concourse of divines in Persia! Be fair concerning that which hath appeared with truth and be not of the oppressors.

order.why: Challenges religious leaders to judge the new Revelation by the same standards used to establish their inherited beliefs.
Ask how learning can conceal the object it seeks.
shortened: Take hold of the reins of the Cause by My Most Great Name and say: O concourse of divines! Fear God and bar not those who were created by God's binding Word, by which the books of the world were detailed, if ye but knew. Beware lest the conditions of learning withhold you from the Known One.

order.why: Read books and the new Book in relation to insight.
Consider the limitations of allusion and acquired learning.
Read the recurrence of learning used against recognition.
Turn attention toward the heart’s reception of knowledge.
shortened: O concourse of divines! Cast aside what ye possess of idle fancies, then turn with your hearts toward the Most Exalted Horizon - the Station from which hath shone forth the Sun of Knowledge from One mighty and powerful.

order.why: Ask why promised knowledge meets resistance.
shortened: Say: O company of the learned! Why have ye turned away from the Dayspring of divine knowledge after having been promised it in the Tablets of God, the All-Knowing, the All-Informed? By My life! They are worshippers of vain imaginings, save him who hath held fast to My Name, the Self-Subsisting, Who hath come with a mighty sovereignty.

order.why: Read expectation beside the arrival of the expected One.
Keep promise and fulfilment together.
shortened: Say: O concourse of divines! Fear ye God and follow not your idle fancies. The Promise hath come and the Promised One calleth aloud before all faces.

order.why: Consider the contradiction between prayer for an advent and harm at its arrival.
shortened: Say: O concourse of divines! Where is the phrase "may God hasten His advent" and where are your supplications and prayers for His appearance and manifestation? Be fair, O people, and be not of the wrongdoers. Ye have pronounced judgment against Him through Whose name your stations were exalted and your ordinances encompassed all and your commands were executed.

order.why: Read attachment to inherited words in its polemical setting.
Hear the call to attend to new speech.
shortened: Say: O high priests! The Possessor of the world is come. His Way is unlike other ways, and His words are unlike other words. Hearken ye unto them and come towards Him. This is the Day of Victory, and no one hath ever witnessed or will again witness its like.

order.why: Consider whose judgement governs interpretation of the Book.
Read the image of human pens before the Supreme Pen.
Ask what inward possessions obstruct reception.
Contrast wealth and conjecture with what endures.
shortened: O concourse of divines! Pride not yourselves on your conjectures and idle fancies, nor on your riches and wealth. Choose for yourselves that which shall endure in the kingdom of your Lord, the Most High, the Mighty, the Great. This is a matter that your power and might cannot weaken, nor your imaginings affect. Fear God and be among the discerning ones.

order.why: Read the warning about pride and a following.
shortened: Amongst the people is he whose learning hath made him proud, and who hath been debarred thereby from recognizing My Name, the Self-Subsisting; who, when he heareth the tread of sandals following behind him, waxeth greater in his own esteem than Nimrod.

Say: O concourse of divines! Hear ye not the shrill voice of My Most Exalted Pen? See ye not this Sun that shineth in refulgent splendour above the All-Glorious Horizon? For how long will ye worship the idols of your evil passions? Forsake your vain imaginings, and turn yourselves unto God, your Everlasting Lord.

order.why: Consider unexamined allegiance and tyranny.
Read the warning that usurped leadership offers no lasting gain.
Place authority beneath divine sovereignty.
Read the particular charge of heedlessness.
Consider the relationship between interpretive veils and injustice.
Keep the criticism of obstruction in its historical and religious setting.
Face the severe denunciation of bloodshed.
shortened: Thus speaks He, blessed and exalted be He: "O concourse of divines! Not one among you at the dawn of the Manifestation attained to faith. You all, along with your ignorant followers, engaged in cursing and denouncing. Throughout ages and centuries, you imagined yourselves to be commemorating God and following His commandments. Yet when the dawn of hope appeared and the blessed Tree sprouted forth, you arose with swords of hatred to cut it down and issued decrees for the shedding of His most pure blood.

Now set aside your ignorant prejudices and speak with justice and fairness. The horizon of the world is illumined and adorned with the lights of the manifestation of Him Who conversed with Moses. Behold Him with His own eyes.

order.why: Read oppression in relation to the sufferings of Moses and Christ.
shortened: Say: O concourse of divines! Fear ye the Lord of Names. He hath come with the truth with a sovereignty that hath conquered all who are in the heavens and earth. Through your oppression the Apostle hath lamented in the Most Exalted Paradise, and the Spirit in the Supreme Kingdom, and the Wronged One in this noble station.

order.why: Retain the warning about imagined certainties.
shortened: O concourse of divines! Fear ye God, and follow not idle fancies and vain imaginings.

order.why: Read the stern expression of wrath as prophetic polemic.
Consider honouring a name while fleeing its bearer.
Read the call to awaken alongside the supplied stern language.
End with the summons to recognize the promised advent.
Retain the declaration concerning religious power.

questions: What responsibilities follow from possessing religious knowledge or influence over others?
How might the same learning become either preparation for recognition or a barrier to it?
What would it mean to apply consistent standards of evidence to familiar and unfamiliar religious claims?
How does Matthew’s concern with ethical substance compare with the appeals to justice and care in these selections?
How can we study forceful prophetic criticism with historical care while examining our own openness to correction?

neighbors.invitation: Examine discernment in the choice to follow a guide.
Consider different levels of understanding without encouraging vain disputes.

references.label: 1 · Matthew 23:23–28 · Authority and weightier obligations
references.note: The passage criticizes meticulous outward observance combined with neglect of judgement, mercy, and faith, and contrasts appearance with inward conduct. Compare its ethical challenge with this compilation’s appeals to fairness and care. Read the rebuke in its own setting, not as a description of all Jewish people or religious teachers.
